descriptionChirho: To plant trees, vineyards, gardens, or other vegetation in the ground for growth, encompassing all literal agricultural uses across all conjugations and inflections.
To plant or establish people firmly in a land or territory, used metaphorically of God settling His people securely, with pronominal object suffixes referring to persons rather than vegetation.
To drive in, pitch, or set up firmly, as in pitching tent-pavilions or fastening nails and stakes, extending the root sense of thrusting into the ground to non-agricultural objects.
